Description: Two FortiGate-VMs (BYOL/PAYG) across two AZs with AWS Gateway Load Balancer integration, plus a customer VPC with per-AZ GWLB endpoints.

AZ1.Description: Availability zone for the first FortiGate.

AZ2.Description: Availability zone for the second FortiGate.

PrivateCidrAz1.Description: Private subnet AZ1, FortiGate port2 and the GWLB.

PrivateCidrAz2.Description: Private subnet AZ2, FortiGate port2 and the GWLB.

CsPublicCidrAz1.Description: Customer public subnet AZ1, holds the AZ1 GWLB endpoint.

CsPublicCidrAz2.Description: Customer public subnet AZ2, holds the AZ2 GWLB endpoint.

InstanceType.Description: Must match Arch; c6g.xlarge is arm, c5.xlarge is x86.

LicenseType.Description: FortiGate-VM licence model; selects the AMI.

KeyName.Description: Existing EC2 key pair for SSH access to the FortiGates.

FortiGateAmiOverride.Description: Optional. Overrides the pinned FortiOS 7.6.7 AMI table, for a region it does not cover or a different build.

LicenseFormat.Description: BYOL delivery: a .lic file. Ignored for payg.

UseS3Bootstrap.Description: Stage the config and licence in an S3 bucket this stack creates instead of inline user-data. Required for licences over the 4096-byte parameter limit.

LicenseSourceBucket.Description: S3 mode with LicenseFormat 'file': existing bucket holding the two .lic files, copied into the bucket this stack creates. CloudFormation cannot upload local files, so they must already be in S3.

LicenseKey1.Description: (BYOL) Licence key in LicenseSourceBucket, for FortiGate 1.  Need to set true for UseS3Bootstrap

LicenseKey2.Description: (BYOL) Licence key in LicenseSourceBucket, for FortiGate 2.  Need to set true for UseS3Bootstrap

Description.Fn::Sub: ${AWS::StackName} - GWLB ENI lookup and FortiGate bootstrap staging

import ipaddress
import logging
import time

import boto3
import cfnresponse

log = logging.getLogger()
log.setLevel(logging.INFO)

ec2 = boto3.client("ec2")
s3 = boto3.client("s3")


def find_gwlb_eni(glob, subnet_id):
    """Private IP of the GWLB's own ENI in one subnet.

    CloudFormation's "*ELB*" filter would also match an unrelated load
    balancer in the same VPC and AZ. This glob is "*" + the load
    balancer's full name, paired with the subnet, so exactly one
    interface can match.
    """
    for _ in range(20):
        found = ec2.describe_network_interfaces(
            Filters=[
                {"Name": "description", "Values": [glob]},
                {"Name": "subnet-id", "Values": [subnet_id]},
            ]
        ).get("NetworkInterfaces", [])
        if found:
            ip = found[0]["PrivateIpAddress"]
            log.info("gwlb eni in %s -> %s", subnet_id, ip)
            return ip
        time.sleep(5)
    raise RuntimeError("no GWLB ENI found in subnet " + subnet_id)


def describe_gwlb_eni(props):
    data = {}
    for n, subnet in enumerate(props["Subnets"], 1):
        data["Ip%d" % n] = find_gwlb_eni(props["DescriptionGlob"], subnet)
    # CloudFormation used cidrhost(cidr, 1). Splitting octets with
    # intrinsics would be wrong for any prefix longer than /24.
    for n, cidr in enumerate(props["Cidrs"], 1):
        data["Gw%d" % n] = str(next(ipaddress.ip_network(cidr).hosts()))
    return data


def fgt_bootstrap(props, request_type):
    """Echo one FortiGate's rendered config, and stage it in S3.

    Returning it through Data["Config"] is what lets the config be
    written once in the template and still reach both delivery paths.
    A custom resource response body is capped at 4096 bytes; the stock
    config uses well under half, but mind that before growing it.
    """
    body = props["ConfigBody"]
    bucket = props.get("Bucket") or ""
    key = props["ConfigKey"]
    source = props.get("LicenseSourceBucket") or ""
    licence = props.get("LicenseKey") or ""

    if not bucket:
        return {"Config": body}

    if request_type == "Delete":
        # CloudFormation cannot delete a bucket that still holds
        # objects, so remove everything this resource put there.
        for gone in [key] + ([licence] if source and licence else []):
            try:
                s3.delete_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=gone)
                log.info("deleted s3://%s/%s", bucket, gone)
            except Exception as exc:
                log.warning("could not delete %s: %s", gone, exc)
        return {"Config": body}

    s3.put_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key, Body=body.encode("utf-8"))
    log.info("wrote s3://%s/%s (%d bytes)", bucket, key, len(body))
    if source and licence:
        s3.copy_object(
            Bucket=bucket,
            Key=licence,
            CopySource={"Bucket": source, "Key": licence},
        )
        log.info("copied s3://%s/%s", source, licence)
    return {"Config": body}


def handler(event, context):
    # Resolved before the try: anything that raises above
    # cfnresponse.send leaves the stack waiting an hour for a reply.
    request_type = event.get("RequestType", "Create")
    physical_id = (event.get("PhysicalResourceId")
                   or event.get("LogicalResourceId", "helper"))
    try:
        props = event["ResourceProperties"]
        action = props["Action"]
        log.info("%s %s (%s)", request_type, action, physical_id)
        if action == "describe-gwlb-eni":
            # Unlike the reference template this re-resolves on
            # Update, so a replaced load balancer is picked up.
            data = {} if request_type == "Delete" else describe_gwlb_eni(props)
        elif action == "fgt-bootstrap":
            data = fgt_bootstrap(props, request_type)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("unknown action " + repr(action))
        cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.SUCCESS, data, physical_id)
    except Exception as exc:
        log.exception("%s failed", request_type)
        # Failing a Delete would strand the stack in DELETE_FAILED.
        status = cfnresponse.SUCCESS if request_type == "Delete" else cfnresponse.FAILED
        cfnresponse.send(event, context, status, {"Error": str(exc)}, physical_id)
